question: Why did the p95 latency go up on 22 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The change in db.pool_size caused the connection pool to be exhausted, leading to increased latency.
why_chain: The db.pool_size was changed from 50 to 5, reducing the number of available connections.
With fewer connections, the pool became exhausted more quickly under normal load.
This exhaustion led to the warning messages seen in the logs.

contributing_factors.description: The increase in request volume did not cause the latency to increase, as the error rate did not change.
why_chain: The request volume remained stable, with a 20% increase in requests.
The error rate also increased by 49%, indicating a different issue.
The warning messages in the logs suggest a connection pool issue.

contributing_factors.description: The error rate increase is not a direct cause of the latency increase, but it could be related to the connection pool exhaustion.
why_chain: The error rate increased by 49%, but the latency increased by 214%.
The connection pool exhaustion is the more immediate cause of the latency increase.
The error rate increase could be due to other factors, such as a different issue with the service.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in latency was due to a sudden spike in traffic.
ruled_out.reason: The request volume did not change significantly, and the error rate did not increase.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in latency was due to a new deployment or version.
ruled_out.reason: There is no evidence of a new release or version being deployed on 22 March 2026.

evidence.summary: P95 latency for service checkout rose from 221 ms to 693 ms (+214%), with a change point at 2026-03-22T13:05:00Z.
The change is concentrated in service checkout: 3 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.02).
At the same time, request volume for service checkout stayed about the same (833 per 5 min before, 997 per 5 min after, +20%).
At the same time, error rate for service checkout rose (0.33% before, 0.49% after, +49%).
Changed checkout db.pool_size from 50 to 5 (all regions) (checkout; 2 min before the change; record R009)
p95 latency above SLO on checkout (checkout; 15 min after the change; record R011)
checkout: WARN connection pool exhausted, waiting for a free connection (checkout, eu-west; 6 min after the change; record R010)
checkout: WARN connection pool exhausted, waiting for a free connection (checkout, ap-south; 20 min after the change; record R012)
checkout: WARN connection pool exhausted, waiting for a free connection (checkout, us-east; 21 min after the change; record R013)

reasons: ✓ A change event (config_changes) lines up in time (2 min before the change).
✓ 4 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✓ Request volume stayed steady, ruling out a traffic spike.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.

actions.action: Review and adjust the db.pool_size configuration to ensure it can handle the current load without exhausting the connection pool.
Implement a connection pool monitoring system to detect exhaustion early and prevent latency spikes.
Monitor the error rate and latency closely to identify any future issues with the connection pool.
